questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Inferior gluteal nerve as a branch of the sacral plexus
questions.question: Which one of the following nerves is a branch of the sacral plexus?

options.D: Lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh.

explanations.A: Correct. The inferior gluteal nerve arises from the sacral plexus, carrying fibres from L5, S1 and S2. It leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen below the piriformis. It then supplies the gluteus maximus, the main extensor of the hip.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The femoral nerve is a branch of the lumbar plexus (L2-L4).
explanations.C: Incorrect. The obturator nerve is a branch of the lumbar plexus (L2-L4).
explanations.D: Incorrect. The lateral cutaneous nerve of the thigh arises from the lumbar plexus (L2-L3).

questions.learning_objective: Identify the inferior gluteal nerve as a sacral plexus branch.

field_notes.keySource: printed KEY ANSWERS table p.10 (Q3 = a)

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Deep artery of the penis as a branch of the internal pudendal artery
questions.question: Which one of the following arteries is a branch of the internal pudendal artery?

explanations.A: Correct. The internal pudendal artery is the chief artery of the perineum. After giving its inferior rectal and perineal branches it ends by supplying the erectile tissue. Its terminal branches are the artery of the bulb, the dorsal artery of the penis and the deep artery of the penis, the last running within the corpus cavernosum.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 'Medial sacral' is not a named branch here; the midline sacral vessel is the median sacral artery, which arises from the abdominal aorta, not the internal pudendal.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The median sacral artery arises from the back of the abdominal aorta just above its bifurcation.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The superior rectal artery is the continuation of the inferior mesenteric artery.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the deep artery of the penis as a branch of the internal pudendal artery.

field_notes.keySource: printed KEY ANSWERS table p.10 (Q4 = a)

questions.subject: renal
questions.title: Arterial supply of the ureter from the gonadal artery
questions.question: Which one of the following arteries gives a blood supply to the ureter?

explanations.A: Correct. The ureter has a segmental blood supply along its whole length. In the abdomen it receives constant branches from the renal and the gonadal (testicular or ovarian) arteries, and in the pelvis from the vesical and uterine arteries. Of the options offered, only the gonadal artery is a recognised ureteric supplier.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The superior vesical artery supplies mainly the upper bladder; it is not the recognised principal ureteric supplier among these options (the lower ureter is supplied more by the inferior vesical/uterine arteries).
explanations.C: Incorrect. The superior mesenteric artery supplies the midgut, not the ureter.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The external iliac artery gives no branch to the ureter; it supplies the lower limb (its branches are the inferior epigastric and deep circumflex iliac arteries).

questions.learning_objective: State that the gonadal (testicular/ovarian) artery contributes to the ureteric blood supply.

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Deep transverse perineal muscle as a content of the deep perineal pouch
questions.question: The deep perineal pouch in the female contains which one of the following?

explanations.B: Correct. The deep perineal pouch lies between the perineal membrane below and the pelvic diaphragm above. It contains the deep transverse perineal muscle and the sphincter urethrae. It also transmits the internal pudendal vessels and the dorsal nerve of the clitoris.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The ischiocavernosus lies in the superficial perineal pouch.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The greater vestibular (Bartholin) glands lie in the superficial perineal pouch in the female.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The bulb of the vestibule lies in the superficial perineal pouch.

questions.learning_objective: Identify the deep transverse perineal muscle as a content of the deep perineal pouch.

field_notes.keySource: printed KEY ANSWERS table p.10 (Q12 = b)

questions.subject: fnd
questions.title: Ischiocavernosus lies in the superficial perineal pouch
questions.question: The ischiocavernosus muscle is found in the:

explanations.B: Correct. The superficial perineal pouch lies between the perineal membrane and the deep perineal fascia. Its three paired muscles are the ischiocavernosus, the bulbospongiosus and the superficial transverse perineal muscle. The ischiocavernosus covers the crus of the penis or clitoris and helps to maintain erection.
explanations.A: Incorrect. It is a perineal, not a true-pelvic, muscle; it lies below the pelvic diaphragm.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The deep perineal pouch contains the deep transverse perineal muscle and sphincter urethrae, not the ischiocavernosus.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The ischiorectal fossa is a fat-filled space lateral to the anal canal; the ischiocavernosus is not one of its contents.

questions.learning_objective: Locate the ischiocavernosus in the superficial perineal pouch.

field_notes.keySource: printed KEY ANSWERS table p.10 (Q15 = b)

questions.subject: gyn
questions.title: Greater vestibular (Bartholin) glands in the superficial perineal pouch
questions.question: Which one of the following structures is present in the superficial perineal pouch in the female?

explanations.C: Correct. In the female the superficial perineal pouch holds the crura and bulbs of the erectile tissue with their muscles. Behind the bulbs of the vestibule lie the greater vestibular (Bartholin) glands. These glands are therefore contents of the superficial, not the deep, perineal pouch.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The sphincter urethrae lies in the deep perineal pouch.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The deep transverse perineal muscle lies in the deep perineal pouch.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The bulbourethral glands are the male homologue and lie in the deep perineal pouch in the male; they are not present in the female.

questions.learning_objective: Locate the greater vestibular glands in the female superficial perineal pouch.
